obligation: FTC notification event (Safeguards Rule)
trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted Finance customer information involving at least 500 consumers. Unauthorized access is presumed to be acquisition unless reliable evidence shows otherwise; data counts as unencrypted if the key was also accessed
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: FTC, electronically on the form at ftc.gov: Finance's name and contact; types of information; date or date range; number of consumers; general description; any law enforcement delay determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Finance (about 34,000 consumers). Holding company staff running Finance's shared services are treated as Finance's agents for discovery
clock_starts: Discovery: first day the event is known to any employee, officer, or other agent of Finance other than the person committing it (314.4(j)(2))
owner: Finance President with the General Counsel

obligation: FTC notice: law enforcement delay
trigger: A law enforcement official gives a written determination that public notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: The FTC notice is still due within 30 days of discovery and must include the determination; law enforcement may request an initial delay of up to 30 days after the FTC notice, extendable by up to 60 days on written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, if law enforcement asks

obligation: Qualified Individual report to Finance's Board of Managers
trigger: Security events and management's responses are material matters for the annual report
deadline: Next annual written report (each September); the Finance President is told the same day under POL-03
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: HIPAA breach risk assessment (four factors), group health plan
trigger: Impermissible acquisition, access, use, or disclosure of plan PHI held by the sponsor, the TPA, or the PBM
deadline: Before deciding not to notify; document as soon as the scope is known
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the self-funded plan is a covered entity
clock_starts: Presumed a breach unless the assessment shows a low probability of compromise
owner: VP of Human Resources (plan Privacy Official) with the General Counsel

obligation: HIPAA breach notice to individuals, group health plan
trigger: Breach of unsecured plan PHI
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Each affected participant and beneficiary by first-class mail (email if agreed); substitute notice if contact information is out of date
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - plan (up to about 1,100 covered persons)
clock_starts: Discovery: first day known, or by reasonable diligence would have been known, to any workforce member or agent of the plan (164.404(a)(2)); sponsor staff doing plan administration count
owner: VP of Human Resources with the General Counsel

obligation: HIPAA notice to media, group health plan
trigger: Breach involving more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction
deadline: Same timing as individual notice
notify: Prominent media outlets serving the state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, if more than 500 residents of one state are affected (a breach of all covered persons would qualify)

obligation: HIPAA notice to HHS, group health plan
trigger: Breach of unsecured plan PHI
deadline: 500 or more: at the same time as individual notice. Fewer than 500: log and report within 60 days after the end of the calendar year
notify: HHS Office for Civil Rights portal
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - plan

obligation: Business associate notice to the plan (TPA, PBM)
trigger: Breach of unsecured plan PHI at the TPA or PBM
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after the business associate's discovery (the BAAs use the same outer limit)
notify: The plan, through the VP of Human Resources
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - inbound duty owed to the plan

obligation: Law enforcement delay, HIPAA
trigger: A law enforcement official states that notice would impede a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period in a written statement; if oral, document it and delay no longer than 30 days unless a written statement follows
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, if law enforcement asks

obligation: Sponsor report of security incidents to the plan
citation: Plan document term required by 45 CFR 164.314(b)(2)(iv) (amendment due 2026-12-31); POL-03 4.6
trigger: Security incident involving plan ePHI held by the sponsor
deadline: Same day under POL-03
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice (holding company to a subsidiary)
trigger: Breach of a system the holding company maintains for a subsidiary (email, files, HRIS, SFTP, warehouse) involving that subsidiary's personal information
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred; POL-03 requires same-day internal notice
notify: The affected subsidiary's President (the covered entity). The agent may send the (3) and (4) notices on its behalf (501.171(6)(b))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the holding company processes personal information for each subsidiary under the intercompany services agreement
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (for example name with SSN, financial account number with access code, health insurance or medical information, or user name or email with password)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. A 15-day extension for good cause, given in writing to the Department within the 30 days, applies to this notice only (501.171(3)(a)). Law enforcement may delay notice by written request (501.171(4)(b))
notify: Affected Florida residents (employees of any group company; Finance borrowers and applicants; Home Services customers; plan members)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - each group company is the covered entity for its own employees and customers
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
owner: Each affected company's President with the General Counsel

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (no extension)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General), with the content listed in 501.171(3)(b)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents (a Finance or plan breach could reach this count)

obligation: Florida deemed compliance under a federal regulator's rules
trigger: Individual notice given under the rules of the covered entity's primary or functional federal regulator
deadline: Copy of that notice to the Department in time
applies_at_this_tier: Possibly for the plan (HIPAA notice); counsel decides whether HHS is the plan's primary or functional federal regulator for this purpose

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

obligation: Other states' breach laws
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Affected employees, borrowers, applicants, or plan members who reside outside Florida
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check residency on the affected list; most are Florida residents, but former borrowers and employees may have moved

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement
citation: FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3); FBI field office; CISA
trigger: Ransomware, extortion, data theft, or fraudulent payment
deadline: As early as possible; for payment fraud, report to the bank first and IC3 the same day
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary; recommended for every severity 1 incident

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring any vendor
notify: Carrier breach hotline ($10 million limit, $200,000 retention)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Crime policy notice (social engineering fraud)
trigger: Fraudulent payment induced by impersonation
deadline: Per policy; notify promptly after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Bank notice of suspected payment fraud or credential compromise
trigger: Fraudulent or suspicious payment; compromise of a treasury user, bank token, or the SFTP server
deadline: Immediately on suspicion; recall requests are time-critical
notify: Bank fraud line and relationship manager
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Lender notice
citation: Senior credit agreement and Finance warehouse line (contracts)
trigger: Event the agreements treat as a material adverse event (counsel confirms the covenant wording)
deadline: Per agreement
applies_at_this_tier: Check with counsel - contractual

obligation: Private equity sponsor notice
trigger: Severity 1 incident
deadline: Within 24 hours of declaration
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: Bank partner notice
trigger: Security incident affecting Finance servicing systems or data on participated loans (from 2027-01)
deadline: Within 72 hours of determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes from 2027-01 - contractual

obligation: Card processor notice
trigger: Suspected compromise of card data at Supply or Home Services
deadline: Per merchant agreement
applies_at_this_tier: Only if card data may be involved (unlikely: point-to-point encrypted devices and a hosted payment page)
owner: Supply President or Home Services President

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05
trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at an SEC registrant
deadline: Within 4 business days after determining materiality
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is not an SEC registrant (P03 section 1)

obligation: Federal Reserve computer-security notification incident
trigger: Notification incident at a bank holding company
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 36 hours after determining a notification incident occurred
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is not a bank holding company (P03 section 1)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then); recheck applicability when final

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or services
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the group holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the group holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
